newsitem.title: UK: Bradies expect more Ecuador gains on Eurobond deal.
newsitem.headline: Bradies expect more Ecuador gains on Eurobond deal.

text.p: Ecuador's Brady bonds did not gain much more ground following the launch of the country's debut Eurobond on Friday but dealers expected further gains at the start of New York trade.
"Ecuador does not trade much in London," a dealer said. "The market is short, so we should see further gains on short-covering in New York, at least by half a point," he added.
He said the extent of the gains would depend on how the Eurobond fared in the secondary market.
Ecuador launched a two-tranche Eurobond for a total of $500 million on Friday via lead manager Chase.
The five-year tranche, for $350 million, is a fixed-rate Eurobond to be priced 470 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
The seven-year tranche, for $150 million, is a floating rate note to be priced at six-month LIBOR plus 475 b.p.
Ecuador PDI rose 1/8 to 57-1/8 bid, while Ecuador IEB rose 1/2 to 84 bid. Ecuador PARS up 1/4 were bid at 41-3/4 and Ecuador DISC up 1/2 were bid at 65-1/8.
"The deal supports the Brady market and therefore we've seen some action in the Bradies," another dealer said. "Ecuador gained strongly on Thursday and I reckon there's more upside today."
Elsewhere in the market dealers said not much was happening.

"Brady markets have been moving up and down with Treasuries but Treasuries have been whipped around by U.S. data which are contradictory and a bit confusing," an analyst said. "Most investors feel there is volatility without direction and therefore they're staying out of the choppy trading," he said.
